title: orient-prebuild
intention: A prebuild orientation instrument: deterministic scans that measure the territory before CC answers, failing over to Hex (through inference_domain, the sole path) only for what no scan answers — built from the start as a learning device whose scans are seeded by Akien's corrections.
why: Three different conclusions from the same data in one morning, every one rooted in a proxy read (word not capability, record not world, narration not thing). Akien: 'we need a prebuild type step ... a script ... that can _fail over to_ hex ... because we'd build from the start as a learning device' — and mid-build: 'absolutely this moves to the top of the queue as it's both how-we-work and foundational-components.' Law 4 pointed at CC: a discipline in CC's habit varies with the model and the hour; a scan does not.
traces_to: Law 4 — physics not policy, applied to CC's own orientation discipline
Law 3 — an orientation is a measurement, not an impression; Hex output is a labeled read, never `measured`
Law 1 — settled territory is walked (scans), not re-derived per question; a recurring deepening becomes a scan
Law 6 — the failover reaches the host only through inference_domain's gate
memory: learns-its-gates — corrections become scans, provenance required by a proof tooth

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate: cairn/tools/orient/proofs/test_orient.py (15 teeth) under the tester's MEASURED netns seal — validations/test_orient.json, green, sealed. Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier.proves_red: mirrors the charter: mention-instead-of-capability; smaller-world-instead-of-refusal; inference laundered as measurement; a scan without dated-correction provenance; an outbound import in orient.py. Wrong-shape signal: if the registry is static three corrections from now, the learning half is hollow and this is a linter.
falsifier.horizon: re-examine when the post-build inspector exists — the shared scans/filters library question (edge e) is decided by evidence then, not now.
